Label leakage from ChEMBL: the labels are public ChEMBL activities, so any model that queries ChEMBL, uses a ChEMBL-pretrained regression head covering the same assay, or uses a public 'autosota' pipeline that ingests ChEMBL can recover test labels. Any pretrained component must be declared with its training-set provenance and checked against the test InChIKeys.

Stereo/salt duplicates: the same compound appears as different SMILES (salts, tautomers, stereo variants) across train and test; nearest-neighbour models then look brilliant. De-duplicate on stereo-stripped InChIKey, not on raw SMILES strings.

Unit confusion: the CSV carries both 'y' (log10 of nM, the training label) and 'y [pEC50/pKi]' (shifted by 9). Scoring against the wrong column leaves MSE unchanged under a pure shift but breaks any mixing of the two, and reporting a number computed in the wrong unit against the leaderboard is a false positive.

Test-set reuse / silent model selection: with 126-733 test molecules, the MSE standard error is roughly 0.05-0.15, so picking the best of many models by test MSE will 'beat' a 0.3-0.5 record by luck. All selection must be out-of-fold on train, the number of test evaluations must be reported, and the 5%-relative + bootstrap margin is mandatory.

Beating only the auto-generated baseline: 'autosota-*' is a machine-produced submission, not the literature state of the art. The NOVELTY skeptic must also compare to the MoleculeACE paper's own published per-target RMSE/MSE table and to any newer activity-cliff paper (e.g. 2023-2026 arXiv/JCIM work citing MoleculeACE) for that same target and split.
targets.statement: Polaris hosts 30 MoleculeACE benchmarks (molecularml/moleculeace-CHEMBL<id>-<Ki|EC50>), one per ChEMBL target from van Tilborg et al., 'Exposing the Limitations of Molecular Machine Learning with Activity Cliffs' (JCIM 2022). Each is a single-task regression of pKi/pEC50 from SMILES with a fixed activity-cliff-stratified train/test split (train 1,0xx-1,9xx, test 126-733 molecules) and main metric mean_squared_error (lower is better). As of 2026-10-13 nearly every one of the 30 leaderboards has exactly ONE entry, an auto-generated 'autosota-moleculeace-<slug>' submission (e.g. chembl2147-ki 0.311, chembl2835-ki 0.166, chembl264-ki 0.342, chembl4203-ki 0.732, chembl233-ki 0.576, chembl231-ki 0.530, chembl287-ki 0.503, chembl237-ec50 0.497); only chembl236-ki and chembl234-ki have 3 entries. The underlying data and the exact split are fully public: MoleculeACE ships one CSV per target (MoleculeACE/Data/benchmark_data/CHEMBL<id>_<Ki|EC50>.csv) with columns smiles, y, cliff_mol and split, and the Polaris train/test sizes match that split column exactly (verified for CHEMBL2147_Ki: 1162 train / 294 test = Polaris 1,162 / 294). So a laptop can train and score offline with no account. The open question per target: can a better descriptor/model combination lower the MSE below the listed best, especially on the cliff_mol subset where the MoleculeACE paper showed all methods degrade?
targets.success_criterion: Pick one named MoleculeACE benchmark (full Polaris slug). Success means a saved prediction file (one predicted y per test molecule, in the official test order, with the benchmark slug, the sha256 of the MoleculeACE CSV used, and the exact test-row indices) such that (a) the test set is EXACTLY the rows with split=='test' in the public MoleculeACE CSV for that target and the label column is the same 'y' column (log10-transformed nM) the Polaris benchmark uses, with the Polaris train/test counts from https://polarishub.io/api/v1/benchmark/molecularml/<slug> matching, (b) the skeptic's own sklearn.metrics.mean_squared_error on that file is strictly LOWER (direction: min) than EVERY mean_squared_error listed in the leaderboard table at https://polarishub.io/benchmarks/molecularml/<slug>, re-fetched live immediately before claiming, (c) the margin is at least 5% relative to the current best AND a paired bootstrap over test molecules (10,000 resamples, same resamples for both prediction sets where the attacker's and a reproduced baseline's predictions are available; otherwise 10,000 resamples of the attacker's squared errors) puts the attacker's MSE below the listed best in at least 95% of resamples, and (d) no test molecule, nor any molecule with the same InChIKey (ignoring stereo) as a test molecule, appeared in training, and no label for a test molecule was looked up from ChEMBL or any other source. The model must be fit on the official train split only; multi-target transfer is allowed only from OTHER MoleculeACE targets' train splits and must be declared, with the union checked for test-molecule leakage.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the MoleculeACE CSV for the target from raw.githubusercontent.com/molML/MoleculeACE/main/MoleculeACE/Data/benchmark_data/<file>.csv, checks sha256 against the manifest, selects split=='test', confirms the count matches nTestDatapoints from https://polarishub.io/api/v1/benchmark/molecularml/<slug>, loads the attacker's prediction vector, recomputes MSE with sklearn, runs the 10,000-resample bootstrap, canonicalises train and test SMILES with RDKit and asserts no InChIKey (stereo-stripped) overlap, then re-fetches the live Polaris leaderboard HTML and parses all listed mean_squared_error values. Optionally re-runs the attacker's training script end-to-end (minutes on CPU for ~1.5k molecules).

angles: Attack the metric directly: AAFE is a geometric-mean absolute error in log space, so train on log10 of the endpoint with an L1 loss, and fit the optimal additive log-space offset (the median log residual) on out-of-fold train predictions; a pure median-offset correction typically removes several percent of AAFE from any mis-scaled model, which is what the 1.013-vs-R2-0.123 pattern implies is available.

Variance-aware shrinkage in log space: predict a log-space mean and variance, then shrink toward the train-set log median proportionally to predicted variance; because AAFE penalises absolute log deviation, shrinking uncertain predictions is near-free improvement.

Metabolism-specific features: CYP3A4 turnover depends on lipophilicity and on the presence of accessible soft spots, so add SMARTS counts for N-dealkylation/O-dealkylation/benzylic-oxidation motifs, logD7.4, aromatic-carbon fraction and fraction-sp3, on top of ECFP; cheap and mechanistically aligned.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing / homomorphic filtering): work entirely in the log domain, where multiplicative assay error becomes additive, apply robust (Huber/Theil-Sen) fitting and median filtering across ensemble members, and convert back only at the end - the textbook treatment for fold-error metrics.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ordinal ECOC): discretise log-clearance into ordered bins with a Hadamard codebook of binary tasks and decode by minimum distance, which stabilises predictions against the heavy assay noise of microsomal turnover data.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / NCD similarity) and CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / fragment n-grams) as uncorrelated ensemble members: parameter-free SMILES-compression kernels and BRICS-fragment n-gram models, combined by inverse-variance fusion.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / abundance-weighted sampling): reweight training compounds by inverse scaffold abundance so that the model is not dominated by a few large analogue series, improving generalisation to the test fold's chemotypes.
targets.name: Polaris novartis/adme-novartis-cyp3a4-reg: beat the listed absolute-average-fold-error on 368 test compounds

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on AAFE under the live-refetch, margin, bootstrap and no-ranking-loss rules.

A calibration-only result: take a reproduced baseline's predictions (the attacker's own re-implementation of a descriptor/boosting model, reported with code), apply a monotone recalibration fit ONLY on out-of-fold train predictions, and show that AAFE drops below the live listed best while Spearman is unchanged to within 0.005 - isolating calibration as the mechanism.

A ranking result: beat the best Spearman listed on the same live table (currently 0.410, MolEncoder) by at least 0.030 with the bootstrap rule satisfied, reported as a scoped metric-specific claim rather than as the benchmark record.

pitfalls: Metric definition drift: AAFE has several variants (geometric mean fold error, 10**mean|log10 ratio|, mean of max(p/t, t/p)). Computing a different variant than Polaris does can swing the number by a lot; the exact Polaris metric implementation must be read and used at verification time, and the attacker must report the formula used.

Zero/negative predictions: AAFE is undefined for non-positive predictions, so clipping choices change the score. The clipping rule must be declared and applied identically to all compared prediction sets.

Metric trade-off masquerading as a record: a log-space offset can lower AAFE while the model's ranking is unchanged or worse. The success criterion's no-Spearman-loss clause exists to prevent claiming a pure scaling trick, and any gain must be reported with all five secondary metrics.

Single fold, 368 rows, heavy-tailed clearance labels: a few extreme compounds dominate, so without the bootstrap a 1-2% AAFE 'improvement' is noise. The number of models the attacker evaluated on the test fold must be disclosed.

Leakage via public CYP3A4 data: Novartis released this set publicly and CYP3A4 turnover data for many of these compounds exist in ChEMBL and vendor collections; an undeclared pretrained ADMET model or an external CYP3A4 table can contain the test labels. Declare provenance and check InChIKeys against the test fold.
Empty-companion confusion: novartis/adme-novartis-cyp3a4-cls has no entries; results there are not records, and classification scores must never be compared against this regression table.
targets.statement: Polaris hosts a Novartis CYP3A4 in vitro metabolism benchmark (novartis/adme-novartis-cyp3a4-reg, created 2024-07-15, 368 test compounds) whose main metric is the pharmacokinetics-specific absolute average fold error (AAFE, lower is better). As of 2026-10-13 the leaderboard has only a handful of entries and they are strikingly weak in absolute terms: rank 1 'adme-novartis-cyp3a4-reg-GIRAFFE' AAFE 1.013 with MAE 0.190, MSE 0.062, R2 0.123, Spearman 0.344, Pearson 0.471; 'MolEncoder' AAFE 1.052 with a HIGHER Spearman (0.410) and Pearson (0.545) and R2 0.066; 'AceProp1' AAFE 1.053, Spearman 0.393. The companion classification benchmark novartis/adme-novartis-cyp3a4-cls lists NO results. R2 near 0.1 with Pearson near 0.5 means the listed models are badly mis-scaled rather than uninformative, i.e. the AAFE record is a calibration problem, not a representation-learning problem - exactly the kind of hill a laptop can take. The benchmark's split indices and the dataset parquet download anonymously from the Polaris public API, so scoring is offline and mechanical.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved prediction file (one prediction per official test row in official order; manifest with the slug, sha256 of the downloaded table.parquet and the exact test index array from https://polarishub.io/api/v1/benchmark/novartis/adme-novartis-cyp3a4-reg) such that (a) the test rows and the label column match the API's split and targetCols exactly, (b) the skeptic's own AAFE - computed with the same definition Polaris uses (10 ** mean(|log10(pred) - log10(true)|) on the endpoint's own scale, read from the Polaris metric implementation at verification time) - is strictly LOWER (direction: min) than EVERY absolute_average_fold_error listed in the live leaderboard table, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement is at least 1.5% relative AND a 10,000-resample bootstrap over the 368 test rows puts the attacker's AAFE below the listed best in at least 95% of resamples, (d) the attacker ALSO reports MAE, MSE, R2, Spearman and Pearson from the same prediction file and does not lose more than 0.02 Spearman against the best Spearman listed on that table (so the win is not a pure fold-error trick that destroys ranking), and (e) fitting used only the official train indices, with every pretrained component and external dataset declared and shown to contain no test-fold molecule by stereo-stripped InChIKey. The empty companion leaderboard novartis/adme-novartis-cyp3a4-cls is explicitly excluded: a first entry there is not a record.
targets.verification_method: Plain curl of the public benchmark API (targetCols, mainMetric, split indices) and of the related dataset's table.parquet via /api/v1/dataset/novartis/...; sha256 check; slice the official test rows; recompute AAFE with the Polaris metric definition plus the five secondary metrics; bootstrap over test rows; confirm the attacker's training indices are a subset of the official train indices and that declared external sources contain no test InChIKey; re-fetch the live leaderboard HTML and parse every listed AAFE and Spearman. 368 test rows and a few thousand training rows make a full retrain minutes of CPU.

angles: Kinase-family multi-task learning: PKIS2 profiles the same compounds across hundreds of kinases, so the legitimate signal is cross-kinase correlation among the benchmarks' own train splits; a multi-task booster or reduced-rank regression over kinase columns (restricted to training rows) exploits this where single-task pretrained encoders cannot.

Heavy-tailed percent-inhibition handling: labels are bounded percentages with a spike near 0; model logit/arcsine-transformed inhibition, or a two-stage hurdle model (active/inactive classifier times conditional magnitude regressor), then invert - directly attacks the MSE records (849 on KIT means the baseline is dominated by a few large errors).

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing / matched filtering and whitening): whiten the fingerprint space by the training covariance and use Fisher-discriminant 'matched filters' per kinase as features; detection-theoretic whitening is well-suited to 100-compound problems where plain distances are noisy.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ECOC over kinase panels): represent each compound's activity across the panel of training kinases as a codeword, train a decoder for the target kinase bit, and use minimum-distance decoding; panel selectivity patterns are exactly an error-correcting code over targets.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / NCD) and CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / fragment n-grams): parameter-free SMILES-compression kernels and BRICS-fragment n-gram naive Bayes as uncorrelated ensemble members for a 74-144-row test set, where diversity beats depth.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / replica averaging with a tuned noise temperature): bagging with deliberate label-noise injection and Boltzmann weighting by out-of-fold error, to manage the bias-variance trade-off on tiny data far better than a single tuned model.

Conformal shrinkage toward the train mean for compounds whose nearest-neighbour distance exceeds a calibrated threshold - a guaranteed-in-expectation MSE/MAE win when the test fold contains novel chemotypes.
targets.name: Polaris PKIS2/PKIS1 kinase benchmarks (EGFR, KIT, RET, LOK-SLK): beat shallow leaderboards on 74-144 test compounds

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on polaris/pkis2-kit-wt-reg-v2, the single-entry regression leaderboard (live best MSE 849.611 / MAE 21.480), with the bootstrap rule satisfied.

A multi-task result: one model trained jointly on the train indices of the EGFR, KIT and RET regression benchmarks that beats the live best on at least two of the three under the same margin rules, with the single-task version of the same model reported for ablation.

A classification-ranking result: on polaris/pkis2-kit-wt-cls-v2 or pkis2-ret-wt-cls-v2, beat the live best PR-AUC by at least 0.020 with a model that also does not lose more than 0.010 ROC-AUC against the best listed ROC-AUC, i.e. a genuine ranking improvement rather than a metric trade.

pitfalls: Empty-leaderboard false win: several PKIS variants (and sibling Polaris benchmarks such as polaris/pkis1-egfr-wt-mut-cls-v2, which shows no leaderboard section) have no entries at all; submitting the first number there is NOT beating a record and must never be claimed as one.

Public-source label leakage: PKIS1/PKIS2 percent-inhibition data are published and also present in ChEMBL, so any external kinase-profiling table or kinase-pretrained model can contain the test compounds' labels for the same kinase. Declared provenance plus InChIKey checks against the test fold are mandatory.

Tiny single fold: with 74-144 test compounds, MAE/MSE standard errors are large (MSE on a heavy-tailed label is dominated by two or three compounds), so a 5%-relative margin plus a bootstrap is the minimum, and the count of models evaluated on the test fold must be disclosed.

v1-vs-v2 confusion: the '*-r-1'/'*-c-1' (2023-12) and '*-reg-v2'/'*-cls-v2' (2024-07) benchmarks share a name but differ in split and sometimes label definition; quoting a v1 record against a v2 result (or vice versa) is an invalid comparison. Always cite the exact slug and its API-reported split.

Metric trade: pkis2 classification tables list accuracy, f1, roc_auc, pr_auc, mcc and cohen_kappa; the benchmark's mainMetric is the only record, and an apparent win on one column with losses elsewhere must be reported as a scoped partial, not a record.

Activity-cliff/duplicate structure overlap between train and test folds (PKIS contains close analogue series); report a 1-NN-on-ECFP baseline as a floor so that a 'win' is not just better memorisation.
targets.statement: Polaris hosts 14 kinase-inhibition benchmarks built from the published PKIS1/PKIS2 chemogenomic sets: regression (percent-inhibition) and classification variants for EGFR wild-type, KIT wild-type, RET wild-type and the LOK/SLK pair, in both a v1 ('*-r-1' / '*-c-1') and a v2 ('*-reg-v2' / '*-cls-v2') formulation, with test sizes of 74-144 compounds. The leaderboards are extremely shallow: polaris/pkis2-kit-wt-reg-v2 has a SINGLE entry (CheMeleon, MAE 21.480, MSE 849.611, R2 0.296, Spearman 0.536), polaris/pkis2-kit-wt-cls-v2 has two (CheMeleon PR-AUC 0.646, MHNfs 0.376), polaris/pkis2-egfr-wt-reg-v2 has a handful (best MAE 16.009 by an 'aether-pharmaos' ensemble), polaris/pkis2-ret-wt-reg-v2 best MAE 18.252-18.309 from 1B/3B MolGPS models, polaris/pkis2-ret-wt-cls-v2 best PR-AUC 0.885, and polaris/pkis1-egfr-wt-mut-cls-v2 shows no leaderboard section at all. Data and explicit split indices download anonymously from the Polaris public API, so everything is scorable offline on a laptop. With 74-144 test compounds and percent-inhibition labels, careful classical QSAR plus variance reduction is directly competitive with the pretrained models that currently hold these rows.
targets.success_criterion: Pick one named Polaris PKIS benchmark whose live leaderboard has at least one entry. Success means a saved prediction file (one prediction per official test row in official order; probabilities for classification; manifest with slug, sha256 of the downloaded table.parquet and the exact test index array from the public API) such that (a) the test rows are exactly the indices in the 'split' field of https://polarishub.io/api/v1/benchmark/polaris/<slug> and the label column is that benchmark's targetCols entry, (b) the skeptic's own computation of the benchmark's mainMetric is strictly better in that metric's direction than EVERY value listed in the live leaderboard table, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the margin is at least 5% relative for MSE/MAE or 0.020 absolute for PR-AUC/ROC-AUC/balanced-accuracy, AND a 10,000-resample bootstrap over the 74-144 test rows puts the attacker ahead in at least 95% of resamples, (d) fitting used only the official train indices, with any multi-task borrowing restricted to OTHER kinases' train indices (declared, and checked to contain no test row of the target benchmark), and (e) no external PKIS or ChEMBL kinase-profiling record for a test compound-kinase pair was used; the PKIS data are public, so this must be verified by InChIKey, not assumed. A first entry on an EMPTY leaderboard is NOT a record and does not count.
targets.verification_method: Plain-curl the public API for the benchmark (targetCols, mainMetric, split indices) and for the related dataset (table.parquet URL on data.polarishub.io), hash-check the parquet, slice the official test rows, recompute the mainMetric with sklearn/scipy from the attacker's prediction file, run the bootstrap, verify the attacker's training indices are a subset of the official train indices and that declared auxiliary data contain no test InChIKey, then re-fetch the live leaderboard page and parse every listed value for that metric. Test sets of 74-144 rows and train sets of a few hundred make full re-training a matter of minutes on CPU.

angles: Single-fold means variance reduction wins: average many models and many featurisations (ECFP/FCFP/Avalon/MACCS/RDKit-2D), each tuned by grouped CV on the train indices only, then combine by out-of-fold-weighted stacking. The listed leaders are single large pretrained models with no ensembling across feature families.

Tabular-foundation-model-style priors on CPU: the leaderboards already contain TabPFNv2 rows, and their numbers are beatable on several benchmarks; running TabPFN-class models over multiple descriptor subsets and aggregating (bagging over feature subspaces) is CPU-feasible at these data sizes and is the most direct route.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression-based similarity): normalised compression distance over canonical SMILES as an SVR/k-NN kernel, used as an ensemble member that errs differently from fingerprint models - parameter-free, no training, seconds of CPU.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing / matched filters): build 'matched filter' templates per activity class from the train set in fingerprint space (class-mean fingerprint, whitened by the within-class covariance - i.e. a Fisher/LDA direction in bit space) and use the filter response as a feature; a classical detection-theory view of substructure alerts.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / rarefaction and abundance weighting): weight training molecules by the inverse 'abundance' of their scaffold in the train set (rarefaction-style) so rare scaffolds are not drowned out, since the test fold is a different scaffold community.
CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ordinal ECOC) for the Spearman and PR-AUC benchmarks: threshold-ensemble decoding to produce a robust ranking rather than a point estimate.

Metric-specific post-processing: for MAE benchmarks, median-calibrate; for PR-AUC, rank-optimise the positive class with a pairwise loss; for Spearman, aggregate ensemble members in rank space (Borda) instead of value space.
targets.name: Polaris tdcommons/* ADMET mirrors: beat the top listed score on a single-fold public split (offline-scorable)

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on one of the tiny-test benchmarks (tdcommons/dili 96, tdcommons/herg 132, tdcommons/cyp2c9-substrate-carbonmangels 135, tdcommons/half-life-obach 135) with the bootstrap rule satisfied.

A no-pretraining result: a model using only RDKit-computable features and classical learners (no pretrained neural encoder, no external labelled data) whose score beats every listed entry that is a large pretrained model (the '1B_MPNN_*', '3B_e50_MPNN_*', 'MolEncoder', 'CheMeleon', 'TabPFNv2-*' rows) on one benchmark, under the same margin and bootstrap rules, even if some other row remains ahead - reported explicitly as a scoped claim.

A cross-benchmark sweep: one fixed recipe (no per-benchmark tuning on test) that beats the live leaderboard best on at least three tdcommons/* Polaris benchmarks at once, each verified against its own live table.

pitfalls: Pretraining contamination is the central trap: these are the standard public TDC/ADMET sets, so '1B_MPNN', 'MolEncoder', 'CheMeleon' and any ADMET-pretrained encoder may have trained on the very molecules in this single test fold, and so may an attacker's chosen pretrained featuriser. Provenance must be declared and InChIKey overlap with the test fold checked; an undeclared pretrained featuriser is grounds to reject the claim outright.

Wrong split: the Polaris fold is NOT the TDC scaffold split (different sizes and indices) and is a single fold, not 5 seeds. Mixing the two protocols - e.g. quoting a TDC 5-seed mean against a Polaris table - is an invalid comparison in both directions.

Single-fold luck: 96-1,478 test rows with one fold means no seed averaging is available; the bootstrap and the absolute/relative margin rules are the only defence, and the number of distinct models the attacker evaluated on the test fold must be reported (any selection on the test fold invalidates the claim).

Metric mismatch: each benchmark has one mainMetric from the API (mean_absolute_error, roc_auc, pr_auc, spearmanr). The leaderboard page may show several columns; beating a non-main metric is not a record, and pr_auc must be computed as average precision exactly as Polaris does.

Label-column confusion in the parquet: several of these datasets carry multiple columns (raw and transformed endpoint values); scoring against a column other than targetCols silently changes the scale.

Novelty trap: the Polaris tables move (new rows appeared through 2025-2026, e.g. 'vidraft-*', 'agentomics-ml-*', 'nextflow-frontier-*' entries), so the table MUST be re-fetched minutes before any claim, and the NOVELTY skeptic must also check for papers reporting the same Polaris fold.
targets.statement: Polaris mirrors 16 TDC ADMET datasets as its own single-task benchmarks (tdcommons/caco2-wang, herg, dili, half-life-obach, vdss-lombardo, clearance-hepatocyte-az, clearance-microsome-az, ld50-zhu, cyp2c9-substrate-carbonmangels, cyp2d6-substrate-carbonmangels, cyp3a4-substrate-carbonmangels, bbb-martins, ames, ppbr-az, lipophilicity-astrazeneca, bioavailability-ma, pgp-broccatelli, solubility-aqsoldb, hia-hou). Unlike TDC these are ONE fixed fold with explicit train/test index lists served by the public API (e.g. caco2-wang 728/182, herg 132 test, dili 96 test, half-life-obach 135 test, cyp2c9-substrate 135 test), and both the table.parquet and the split indices download anonymously over plain HTTPS (verified: https://data.polarishub.io/dataset/polaris/adme-fang-1/table.parquet returned 200 and /api/v1/benchmark/<slug> returns the explicit test index array), so a laptop can score locally with no account and no submission. Leaderboards are active but shallow and dominated by big pretrained models: tdcommons/herg best ROC-AUC 0.915, tdcommons/dili 0.950, tdcommons/caco2-wang MAE 0.270, tdcommons/half-life-obach Spearman 0.625, tdcommons/vdss-lombardo Spearman 0.726, tdcommons/clearance-hepatocyte-az Spearman 0.538, tdcommons/ld50-zhu MAE 0.526, tdcommons/cyp2c9-substrate-carbonmangels PR-AUC 0.478. Single-fold scoring on 96-1,478 test molecules means a careful classical model has a real shot, and the frontier is per-benchmark.
targets.success_criterion: Pick one named Polaris tdcommons benchmark. Success means a saved prediction file (one prediction per official test row in the official order, probabilities in [0,1] for classification, manifest with the benchmark slug, the sha256 of the downloaded table.parquet, and the exact test index array) such that (a) the test rows are exactly the indices in the 'split' field of https://polarishub.io/api/v1/benchmark/tdcommons/<slug> and the label column is that benchmark's targetCols entry, (b) the skeptic's own computation of the benchmark's mainMetric (sklearn: mean_absolute_error, roc_auc_score, average_precision for pr_auc, scipy.stats.spearmanr) is strictly better in the metric's own direction than EVERY value listed in the live leaderboard table at https://polarishub.io/benchmarks/tdcommons/<slug>, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the margin is at least 3% relative for error metrics, or at least 0.010 absolute for ROC-AUC / PR-AUC / Spearman, AND a 10,000-resample bootstrap over test rows puts the attacker's value ahead of the listed best in at least 95% of resamples, (d) the model was fit only on the official train indices (internal validation carved from them), and (e) the attacker declares every pretrained component with its training-data provenance and shows that no test molecule (stereo-stripped InChIKey) appears in any declared training source - which, since these are standard public ADMET sets, must be checked rather than assumed. Reporting a different metric from the benchmark's mainMetric, or a different split, does not count.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic calls https://polarishub.io/api/v1/benchmark/tdcommons/<slug> with plain curl (public, no auth), reads targetCols, mainMetric and the split index arrays, downloads the related dataset's table.parquet from the data.polarishub.io URL given by /api/v1/dataset/tdcommons/<slug>, checks its sha256 against the manifest, slices the official test rows, loads the attacker's prediction vector, recomputes the mainMetric with sklearn/scipy, runs the bootstrap, checks train/test InChIKey disjointness and that the attacker's training indices are a subset of the official train indices, then re-fetches the live leaderboard HTML and parses every listed value. Everything fits in minutes on CPU.

angles: Do classical docking properly: exhaustive sampling budgets, multiple independent runs per complex with different seeds, careful protonation/tautomer enumeration of the ligand, receptor protonation and metal/cofactor handling, and consensus pose selection across runs - the PoseBusters paper's own message is that disciplined Vina beats learned methods, and most of the remaining failures are preparation failures.

Consensus re-scoring: generate many poses with one engine and re-rank with an ensemble of independent scoring functions plus a posebusters-style validity prefilter, selecting the top pose that is both well-scored and physically valid; selecting for validity before RMSD is exactly what the PB-valid metric rewards.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing / matched filtering on grids): precompute receptor interaction-field grids and match ligand pharmacophore 'templates' by cross-correlation (FFT-based docking, as used in protein-protein docking) to seed local optimisation, giving broader coverage of the pocket per CPU second than stochastic search alone.

CROSS-DOMAIN (combinatorial search / cryptanalytic restart strategies): treat torsion angles and rigid-body placement as a discrete-continuous key and run tabu-guided simulated annealing with many short restarts and an elite archive instead of one long stochastic run - a better use of a fixed CPU budget.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / replica exchange): parallel-tempered pose sampling across temperatures to cross torsional barriers that single-temperature Monte Carlo misses, then quench the best replicas.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / covering codes): place starting conformers so that they form a covering code over the pocket's rigid-body and torsional space, guaranteeing a bounded distance from any true pose rather than relying on random initialisation.

Template transfer from non-test structures: for each test receptor, find homologous holo structures NOT in the benchmark and transfer their cognate ligand's binding-mode restraints (shape overlap), which is legitimate as long as no test complex's own crystal pose is used - and must be declared explicitly.
targets.name: PoseBusters benchmark set (428 complexes): raise the PB-valid RMSD<=2A redocking rate above the published classical-docking rate

partial_wins.statement: A reproduction artefact: the attacker's own end-to-end harness (download, prepare, dock, score with the official posebusters package) reproducing a published classical-docking PB-valid rate on all 428 systems to within 2 percentage points, with runtime reported - valuable infrastructure, reported as a reproduction and not a record.

A subset result: a strictly higher PB-valid RMSD<=2A rate than the attacker's own reproduced baseline (same inputs, same scorer, margin >= 5 percentage points, bootstrap-confirmed) on a declared, pre-registered subset of at least 150 complexes selected by a rule that does not use the crystal pose (e.g. ligand heavy-atom count below a threshold, or single-chain receptors).

A failure-mode map: a per-complex table showing, for the attacker's method and its reproduced baseline, which posebusters checks fail (clash, internal geometry, stereochemistry, RMSD) with counts, identifying at least one systematic, fixable failure class and demonstrating the fix raises the overall rate - independently checkable from the published pose files.

pitfalls: Empty-leaderboard false win: polaris/posebusters-v1 lists no results, so a first submission is NOT a record. The operative bar is the published rate plus the attacker's own reproduced baseline, and this must be stated in any claim.

Crystal-pose leakage, the signature failure of this field: defining the docking box, the pocket centre, the ligand conformer, or any restraint from the test complex's own crystal ligand inflates success enormously. The box/pocket rule must be uniform, pose-independent and published, and the skeptic must check the run script for it.

Holo-receptor and preparation leakage: using the holo receptor is standard for redocking but must be declared, as must any use of the deposited ligand's protonation/tautomer state; silently taking the crystal ligand's exact protomer is a subtle form of leakage.

Scorer drift: posebusters versions, modes (redock vs dock vs mol) and RMSD conventions (symmetry-corrected or not, heavy atoms only) change the rate by several points. The package version and mode must be pinned in the manifest and re-run by the skeptic, not taken from the attacker's output.

Subset substitution: quietly dropping complexes that fail preparation, or scoring on fewer than all 428 systems, inflates the rate. The denominator must be all 428 systems, with failures counted as failures, unless a pre-registered subset partial win is being claimed.

Benchmark-set contamination for learned components: any learned scoring or pose-prediction component trained on PDB structures released after 2021 may have seen these very complexes; provenance and training cutoffs must be declared, which is also how the PoseBusters paper frames its own fairness analysis.
targets.statement: PoseBusters (Buttenschoen, Morris & Deane, Chem. Sci. 2024) is the standard physics-aware pose-validity benchmark: 428 carefully selected protein-ligand crystal complexes released since 2021, with an open-source scorer (the posebusters pip package / github.com/maabuu/posebusters) that checks chemical validity, intramolecular geometry, intermolecular clashes and RMSD to the crystal pose, and the headline metric is the fraction of predictions that are both RMSD<=2A and 'PB-valid'. The paper's finding - that classical docking (AutoDock Vina) beats deep-learning co-folding and pose-prediction methods on PB-valid rate - makes this an unusual benchmark where CPU docking is the method to beat, not a handicap. Polaris mirrors the set as polaris/posebusters-v1 (428 test systems, main metric rmsd_coverage) and that leaderboard currently lists NO results, while the related plinder-org/runs-n-poses preview table shows how weak the co-folding field is on a harder split (AlphaFold3 15.1% success, Boltz-1 5.6%, Chai-1 4.7%, Protenix 1.5%). The data are public (Zenodo record 8278563, 200 OK) and the Polaris dataset parquet/zarr download anonymously, so a laptop can redock all 428 systems with open-source docking in hours and score with the official package.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved set of predicted ligand poses (one SDF per complex for all 428 PoseBusters systems, plus the receptor files used and a manifest with the sha256 of every input structure, the exact method, software versions, seeds and total wall-clock CPU time) such that (a) the skeptic, running the official posebusters package (version pinned in the manifest) with the standard redock configuration on the attacker's SDFs against the crystal ligands from the public PoseBusters distribution, obtains a PB-valid RMSD<=2A rate that is strictly HIGHER (direction: max) than BOTH (i) every entry listed in the live leaderboard table at https://polarishub.io/benchmarks/polaris/posebusters-v1 , re-fetched immediately before claiming - a first entry on an empty table is explicitly NOT a record - and (ii) the attacker's OWN reproduction, with the same inputs and the same scorer, of a documented classical docking baseline (e.g. AutoDock Vina with a declared box and exhaustiveness), reported with its rate, and (iii) the best PB-valid RMSD<=2A rate for the same 428-system benchmark reported in the PoseBusters paper and in any paper found by the NOVELTY skeptic from the last 24 months, (b) the margin over (ii) and (iii) is at least 3 percentage points and a paired bootstrap over the 428 complexes (10,000 resamples) confirms superiority in at least 95% of resamples, (c) no crystal ligand pose, crystal-ligand coordinates, or ligand-pose-derived restraint for a test complex was used as input - only the receptor structure (holo or declared apo), the ligand's 2D/SMILES identity, and the binding-site definition rule, which must be stated and applied uniformly (e.g. derived from a non-test cognate ligand or from a pocket-detection algorithm, never from the test ligand's own coordinates), and (d) the pose files, the run script and the posebusters output table are published so the whole rate can be recomputed from scratch.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the PoseBusters benchmark set from its public distribution (Zenodo record 8278563 / the posebusters repo), checks input sha256s against the manifest, installs the pinned posebusters package, runs the official 'redock' mode on the attacker's 428 SDFs against the crystal ligands, and reads the PB-valid and RMSD<=2A columns to recompute the rate; repeats the same scoring on the attacker's reproduced baseline poses; runs the paired bootstrap; verifies from the run script that no test-complex crystal ligand coordinates entered pose generation or box definition; and re-fetches the live Polaris leaderboard table. Scoring 428 poses takes minutes; re-docking 428 complexes on 10 CPU cores is hours.

angles: AUPRC-matched training: optimise average precision directly with a pairwise/listwise ranking loss restricted to positive-negative pairs, or use focal/asymmetric loss with prevalence-matched reweighting; log-loss-trained boosters leave AUPRC on the table at these class ratios.

Multi-task across the three CYP inhibition datasets (train_val only): the same compounds and the same qHTS platform underlie all three, so a shared-representation multi-task booster or a stacked model that uses the other two endpoints' out-of-fold predictions as features is both legitimate and cheap.

Feature-union stacking at scale: hashed ECFP4/6, FCFP, Avalon, MACCS, RDKit 2D, plus atom-pair and topological-torsion counts, each fed to its own LightGBM, then stacked by logistic regression on scaffold-grouped out-of-fold predictions - the straightforward way to pass a single MapLight+GNN entry.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ECOC over related endpoints): build codewords from the three inhibition labels plus the three substrate labels and decode the target bit by minimum-distance decoding, which extracts cross-endpoint redundancy as error correction.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / graph diffusion and belief propagation): construct a similarity graph over all molecules (structures only) and run label propagation from train_val labels as an additional transductive feature; diffusion handles scaffold-split shift better than i.i.d. learners and costs seconds.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / NCD) as an ensemble member, and CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / SMILES BPE n-grams with tf-idf) as a second orthogonal view; both are fast enough at 13k molecules and decorrelate the errors of fingerprint models.

Threshold-free calibration and rank aggregation across seeds: average predictions in rank space (Borda) across seeds and model families, which is the right aggregation for a ranking metric like AUPRC.
targets.name: TDC ADMET CYP inhibition leaderboards (CYP2C9/CYP2D6/CYP3A4_Veith, 12-13k molecules, AUPRC): beat MapLight+GNN

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on CYP2D6_Veith (live rank 1 0.790), the weakest of the three records and the one with the largest rank-1-to-rank-2 gap.

A reproduction-plus-margin result on any of the three: an independently re-implemented MapLight-style baseline (fingerprints + RDKit descriptors + gradient boosting, code and features reported) whose 5-seed mean AUPRC is within 0.005 of the live rank-1 value, PLUS an ablated addition that pushes it above the live rank-1 value under the margin rule.

A low-prevalence-slice result: AUPRC restricted to the test molecules outside the 10 most populous Bemis-Murcko scaffolds (count reported, at least 500 molecules) that exceeds the pooled live rank-1 value, evidencing generalisation rather than scaffold memorisation.

pitfalls: Assay-source leakage: the Veith CYP inhibition labels come from a public PubChem qHTS assay, so downloading that assay (or using a model pretrained on it, including several public ADMET predictors) recovers test labels exactly. This is the single most likely false positive; provenance declarations and InChIKey checks are mandatory.

Scaffold-split mis-tuning and re-splitting: hyper-parameters chosen under random CV are mis-set for a scaffold-split test set, and locally regenerated scaffold splits are incomparable. Use group.get() and scaffold-grouped internal CV.

Metric swap: these three are scored by AUPRC (TDC uses AUPRC where positives are scarce). Reporting AUROC - which is much higher and less sensitive - as if it were the record is an easy, invalid 'win'.

Seed cherry-picking against near-zero listed stds (0.000-0.003): the leaderboard value is a 5-seed mean, so the margin must exceed both stds and the bootstrap must pass; CYP3A4's 0.916 +- 0.000 in particular leaves no room for sloppy reporting.

Duplicate/salt-form leakage across the scaffold boundary within TDC itself: report the stereo-stripped InChIKey overlap between train_val and test, and a 1-NN-on-ECFP baseline as a floor, so a 'win' is distinguishable from better memorisation.

Novelty trap: MapLight, ADMET-AI, MiniMol, ZairaChem and 2024-2026 tabular/pretrained submissions report numbers on these exact splits; the NOVELTY skeptic must check the last 24 months for a higher published AUPRC on the same benchmark before any claim.
targets.statement: Three TDC ADMET benchmarks are large enough for real modelling yet still topped by a classical fingerprint+GNN hybrid: CYP2C9_Veith (12,092 molecules, AUPRC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.859 +- 0.001, rank 2 ContextPred 0.839 +- 0.003), CYP2D6_Veith (13,130, AUPRC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.790 +- 0.001, rank 2 ContextPred 0.739 +- 0.005) and CYP3A4_Veith (12,328, AUPRC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.916 +- 0.000, rank 2 ContextPred 0.904 +- 0.002). The protocol is the group's scaffold split with 5 seeds and mean +- std from group.evaluate; the leaderboard pages are undated and the TDC repo's last commits are April 2025. CYP2D6 is the obvious target: rank 1 is 0.051 AUPRC above rank 2, the task is a well-defined qHTS inhibition readout from a single PubChem assay (Veith et al.), and 13k molecules with fingerprint features is minutes per fit on 10 CPU cores, so hundreds of model variants can be explored honestly inside train_val.
targets.success_criterion: Pick one of the three datasets. Success means 5 saved prediction files (seeds 1-5 from tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group, no re-splitting, official test order, probabilities in [0,1], manifest with sha256 of the test SMILES and labels) such that (a) the test split is byte-identical to the group's own, (b) the mean AUPRC over the 5 seeds, recomputed by the skeptic through the group's own evaluate call, is strictly HIGHER (direction: max) than the rank-1 AUPRC in the live leaderboard table for that dataset at tdcommons.ai, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement exceeds max(listed rank-1 std, attacker's own 5-seed std) and is at least 0.005 absolute, with a stratified 10,000-resample bootstrap over test molecules putting the attacker ahead in at least 95% of resamples, (d) fitting used only the official train_val rows of that seed, and (e) no external PubChem/ChEMBL record of the SAME assay endpoint for any test molecule was used, and every pretrained component is declared with provenance and shown to be free of the test molecules by stereo-stripped InChIKey. Transfer from the other two CYP inhibition datasets' train_val rows is allowed if declared and leakage-checked.
targets.verification_method: PyTDC admet_group; group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5; hash-check the test SMILES and labels against the manifest; load the attacker's 5 probability vectors; call group.evaluate for AUPRC mean/std; apply margin and bootstrap rules; verify the attacker's training rows are the official train_val rows and InChIKey-disjoint from test; re-fetch the live leaderboard page and parse every listed AUPRC. A full 5-seed retrain on 12-13k molecules with fingerprint features must be shown to run in under an hour on 10 CPU cores.

angles: Optimise the metric that is actually scored: train with a differentiable rank surrogate (pairwise logistic / LambdaRank-style objective over train_val pairs, or SoftRank) instead of MSE. Spearman is invariant to monotone transforms, so rank-learning models have a structural advantage nobody on these four leaderboards appears to have used.

Physiology-informed features for PK endpoints: fraction unbound proxies, ionisation state at pH 7.4 (acid/base/zwitterion class from pKa predictions), logD7.4, molecular volume, and the classic Lombardo VDss descriptor set; plus known mechanistic couplings (VDss and plasma protein binding, half-life ~ VDss/clearance) as engineered ratio features.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / rank-abundance statistics): model the endpoint as a rank-abundance curve and fit a copula between descriptor-space neighbourhood rank and label rank; copula/rank-transform regression is distribution-free and directly maximises monotone association, which is exactly Spearman.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ordinal ECOC): discretise the endpoint into K ordered bins, train binary classifiers for every threshold (and for Hadamard-coded bin subsets), and decode a rank score by minimum-distance decoding; threshold ensembles are robust to the heavy label noise of hepatocyte/microsome clearance assays.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / cavity-style resampling): bagged ensembles over scaffold-grouped bootstrap replicas with a Boltzmann weighting by out-of-fold Spearman, to pick a 'temperature' (regularisation) that maximises the rank statistic rather than squared error.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing): treat the 5 seeds as repeated measurements of one noisy channel and average predictions in rank space (Borda/Kemeny aggregation across seeds and across model families) rather than in label space; rank-space aggregation is the right estimator for a rank metric and is free.

Transfer from the other three endpoints and from related public PK data (declared, InChIKey-filtered), since half-life, hepatocyte clearance and microsome clearance are mechanistically coupled; multi-task gradient boosting with endpoint one-hots is a few CPU-minutes.
targets.name: TDC ADMET Spearman leaderboards (Half_Life_Obach, Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ, Clearance_Microsome_AZ, VDss_Lombardo): beat rank 1

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ, where the gap between rank 1 (0.536) and rank 2 (0.498) is the largest of the four and the metric is most noise-dominated - verified live at https://tdcommons.ai/benchmark/admet_group/17clhepa/ .

A monotone-physiology result: a model whose predictions for one of the four endpoints are generated from a small, interpretable set of mechanistically motivated descriptors (<= 20 features, named) and still beat the live rank-1 Spearman under the same margin rule - a genuine 'small model beats leaderboard' claim, with the feature list and fitted signs reported.

A cross-endpoint multi-task win: one single multi-task model (trained jointly on the official train_val splits of all four Spearman endpoints, same seed, no test rows) that beats the live rank-1 value on at least two of the four datasets simultaneously under the same margin rule.

pitfalls: Seed and ties manipulation: with 135-243 test molecules, the Spearman standard error is roughly 0.05, far larger than the leaderboard's quoted 5-seed std; best-of-N-seeds or best-of-N-models reporting will cross any of these records by chance. Enforce the full 5-seed mean, the std-based margin and the permutation test.

Scaffold leakage via pretrained descriptors: these endpoints are inside widely used ADMET training collections (ADMET-AI, ZairaChem, commercial descriptor servers), so a pretrained predictor may have seen the exact test molecules and their labels. Declared provenance plus InChIKey overlap checks are mandatory.

Re-splitting / wrong split convention: the four benchmarks use TDC's scaffold split with a 20% test fraction produced by group.get(); regenerating it locally (different RDKit, different seed) silently changes the test set.

Metric substitution: reporting Pearson or R^2 (or Spearman on log-transformed labels of a different unit) instead of the group's Spearman. Only the group's own evaluate output counts, and VDss/clearance unit conventions (L/kg, uL/min/1e6 cells, mL/min/g) must match TDC's.

Measurement-duplicate leakage: Obach half-life and the AZ clearance sets contain the same drugs measured in multiple assays and the same chemical series across train/test; a 1-nearest-neighbour baseline already scores deceptively high, so any claim must beat an explicitly reported 1-NN-on-ECFP baseline as a sanity floor.

Novelty trap: 2024-2026 submissions and papers (MiniMol, CFA, MapLight variants, TabPFN-style tabular models) may already report higher Spearman on these same splits than the stale table; the NOVELTY skeptic must check the last 24 months of literature naming the dataset.
targets.statement: Four TDC ADMET benchmarks are scored by Spearman correlation on a fixed scaffold split, 5 seeds: Half_Life_Obach (667 molecules, rank 1 'CFA' 0.576 +- 0.025, runner-up MapLight 0.562 +- 0.008), Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ (1,020, rank 1 'CFA' 0.536 +- 0.020, runner-up MapLight+GNN 0.498 +- 0.009), Clearance_Microsome_AZ (1,102, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.630 +- 0.010, runner-up MiniMol 0.628 +- 0.005) and VDss_Lombardo (1,130, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.713 +- 0.007, runner-up MapLight 0.707 +- 0.009). TDC itself notes Spearman is used for 'benchmarks that depend on factors beyond the chemical structure', i.e. these are rank-only, noisy, small-data PK endpoints where classical descriptor models already hold the top spots and the per-seed std is 0.005-0.025. The leaderboards carry no dates and the TDC repo's latest commits are April 2025. Open question: can a CPU-only model push the 5-seed mean Spearman above the listed rank-1 value on any of the four?
targets.success_criterion: Pick one of the four datasets. Success means 5 saved prediction files (seeds 1-5 from tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group, no re-splitting, official test order, manifest with sha256 of the test SMILES list) such that (a) the test split is byte-identical to the group's own, (b) the mean Spearman over the 5 seeds, recomputed by the skeptic through the group's own evaluate call, is strictly HIGHER (direction: max) than the rank-1 value in the live leaderboard table for that dataset at tdcommons.ai, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement exceeds max(listed rank-1 std, attacker's own 5-seed std) and is at least 0.010 in absolute Spearman, (d) a permutation test over test molecules (10,000 permutations) rejects equality with the listed rank-1 value at p<0.05 given the test size, and (e) training used only the official train_val rows for that seed, with any external data declared and shown to have zero stereo-stripped-InChIKey overlap with the test split.
targets.verification_method: As for the MAE leaderboards: PyTDC admet_group, group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5, hash-check the test SMILES, load the attacker's 5 prediction vectors, call group.evaluate to get mean/std Spearman, apply the margin and permutation-test rules, then re-fetch the live leaderboard page and parse every listed Spearman. Spearman only needs the predicted ranking, so the skeptic must additionally confirm the prediction vector has no ties-by-construction tricks (e.g. constant blocks) that inflate the statistic, and should re-run the attacker's script for all 5 seeds (minutes to an hour on CPU at 667-1,130 molecules).

angles: Descriptor-space brute force on CPU: RDKit 2D + Mordred-style descriptors + several fingerprint families, feature selection by out-of-fold permutation importance, then LightGBM/CatBoost/ExtraTrees/kernel-ridge stacked with a non-negative least-squares meta-learner fit on out-of-fold predictions of train_val only. The current leaders are exactly this class of model, so the gap is engineering, not scale.

Scaffold-aware internal validation: because the official split is scaffold-based, use Bemis-Murcko-grouped CV inside train_val (GroupKFold on scaffolds) for every hyper-parameter choice; models tuned under random CV are systematically mis-tuned for this test set, which is a cheap, often-ignored 1-3% MAE.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing / robust statistics): MAE is an L1 target while most boosters optimise L2. Train with Huber/quantile (median) objectives, and post-process with an isotonic or median-calibrated mapping fit out-of-fold, which reduces MAE even when correlation is unchanged - directly exploiting the metric rather than the chemistry.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / species-distribution thinking): treat each molecule as a site described by physicochemical 'environment' variables (logP, TPSA, charge state at pH 7.4, H-bond counts) and fit a Gaussian-process / GAM 'response surface' with monotonicity constraints from known permeability and plasma-protein-binding physiology; mechanistic monotone priors buy accuracy where data are sparse (Caco2, PPBR).

CROSS-DOMAIN (combinatorial search / cryptanalytic hill climbing): treat the recipe (descriptor blocks, transforms, model family, loss, calibration) as a discrete string and run a scaffold-CV-scored simulated-annealing/genetic search over it with a strict evaluation budget, exactly as one would search key schedules - CPU-cheap on 1-8k molecules and far more thorough than hand-tuning.

Target transforms: for PPBR (percent bound, 0-100) model logit(fraction unbound) and invert; for LD50 model the log-dose directly but weight by assay-duplicate counts. Inverting a variance-stabilised transform is a classic few-percent MAE gain that leaderboard entries often skip.

Semi-supervised use of unlabelled chemical space: self-training / pseudo-labelling on a large unlabelled set (ZINC/ChEMBL structures only, no labels) to regularise the feature space, with explicit InChIKey filtering against the test split.
targets.name: TDC ADMET Benchmark Group, MAE regression leaderboards (Caco2_Wang, PPBR_AZ, LD50_Zhu): beat rank 1 on the official scaffold split

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on Caco2_Wang alone (906 molecules, smallest and stalest of the three), verified against the live table at https://tdcommons.ai/benchmark/admet_group/01caco2/ .

A reproduction-plus-margin result: an independently re-implemented runner-up-class baseline (plain XGBoost or Chemprop-RDKit) plus a declared, ablated addition (e.g. a conformal shrinkage step or a new descriptor block) whose 5-seed mean MAE beats the live rank-1 value on one dataset, with an ablation table showing the addition, not the baseline, produced the gain.
A strict win on any OTHER TDC ADMET regression leaderboard listed on the group overview page (Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca MAE, Solubility_AqSolDB MAE) under the identical protocol and margin.

pitfalls: Re-splitting instead of using the group's split: the TDC scaffold split must come from group.get(); any locally generated scaffold split (different RDKit version, different seed, different 80/10/10 convention) gives an incomparable number. The skeptic must hash the test SMILES list.

Seed cherry-picking: the leaderboard value is a mean over 5 seeds with a listed std. Reporting the best of 5 seeds, or using fewer seeds, is the single most common false positive here; the margin must exceed the larger of the two stds.

Scaffold leakage through pretraining: ADMET-pretrained models and public descriptor services (and some AutoML submissions) were trained on datasets that INCLUDE Caco2_Wang / PPBR_AZ / LD50_Zhu rows, so the official 'test' molecules are inside their training data. Any pretrained component must have declared provenance and be checked for test-molecule overlap.

Duplicate/near-duplicate molecules inside TDC itself (salts, tautomers, repeated measurements) crossing the scaffold boundary; a nearest-neighbour or memorising model then scores unrealistically well. Check stereo-stripped InChIKey overlap between train_val and test and report it.

Metric mismatch: TDC uses MAE for these three and Spearman for others; computing MAE on standardised/z-scored labels, or on a different unit (log10 cm/s vs cm/s for Caco2, percent vs fraction for PPBR), silently changes the number. Score only through the group's own evaluate call.

Novelty trap: published papers (ADMET-AI, MapLight, ZairaChem, CaliciBoost, MiniMol and 2024-2026 TabPFN-style submissions) report numbers on these same splits that may be better than the stale leaderboard row; the NOVELTY skeptic must search the last 24 months for the same benchmark name before any win is called.
targets.statement: The Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET Benchmark Group fixes, for each of 22 datasets, a scaffold split (20% test) and an evaluation protocol: train with 5 seeds, report mean +- std of the metric through tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group.evaluate_many. The three MAE regression leaderboards with small-to-medium data are Caco2_Wang (906 molecules, rank 1 'CaliciBoost' MAE 0.256 +- 0.006, runner-up 'XG Boost' 0.274 +- 0.004 with 21 parameters), PPBR_AZ (1,797, rank 1 'Gradient Boost' 7.440 +- 0.024 with a single reported parameter, runner-up MapLight+GNN 7.526 +- 0.106) and LD50_Zhu (7,385, rank 1 'BaseBoosting KyQVZ6b2' 0.552 +- 0.009, runner-up ADMETrix 0.573 +- 0.010). All three leaders are classical gradient-boosting / descriptor models, i.e. no GPU is needed to be competitive, and the TDC leaderboard pages carry no dates while the TDC GitHub repo's last commits are from April 2025, so the tables are stale. The open question per dataset: can a better featurisation + ensembling recipe lower the 5-seed mean MAE below the listed rank-1 value?
targets.success_criterion: Pick one of the three datasets. Success means saved per-seed prediction files (5 files, seeds 1-5 as produced by tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group with the default path and no re-splitting, each giving one predicted value per official test molecule in the official order, plus a manifest with the sha256 of the downloaded TDC data files and of the train_val/test SMILES lists) such that (a) the test set is byte-identical to the group's own test split for that benchmark, (b) the mean MAE over the 5 seeds, recomputed by the skeptic with the group's own evaluate call, is strictly LOWER (direction: min) than the rank-1 MAE in the live leaderboard table at the dataset's tdcommons.ai page, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement is at least max(the listed rank-1 std, the attacker's own std across the 5 seeds) and at least 1.5% relative, (d) every model is fit only on the official train_val rows of that same seed (any internal validation must be carved out of train_val), and (e) no external dataset containing any test molecule's measured endpoint is used; if an external training set is used at all, the attacker must list it and show zero stereo-stripped-InChIKey overlap with the test split. Beating only the runner-up does not count.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic pip-installs PyTDC, instantiates admet_group(path='data/'), calls group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5 exactly as the submission instructions prescribe, checks the test SMILES list sha256 against the attacker's manifest, loads the 5 prediction files, calls group.evaluate_many / evaluate to obtain mean and std, confirms the margin rule, then re-fetches the dataset's leaderboard page and parses all listed MAE values. Re-running the attacker's training script for all 5 seeds must fit in under an hour on 10 CPU cores (906-7,385 molecules).

angles: Metric-matched training: for the AUPRC benchmarks optimise a precision-recall surrogate (weighted/focal loss, AP-surrogate, or direct ranking loss on positive-negative pairs) rather than log-loss; with 30-60 positives in the test set, ranking the positives above the ambiguous middle is what moves AUPRC.

Substrate-specific mechanistic features: CYP substrate recognition depends on site-of-metabolism accessibility, so add SMARTS counts for known soft spots (N-dealkylation, O-demethylation, aromatic hydroxylation motifs), partial charges on candidate atoms, and SASA-like proxies from a single fast 3D embedding - cheap on 667 molecules and orthogonal to fingerprints.

CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / morphological parsing): parse SMILES into substituent 'morphemes' (BRICS/RECAP fragments) and build a fragment-presence language model per class, scoring molecules by log-likelihood ratio - a naive-Bayes-over-fragments classifier that is strong exactly when data are tiny and labels noisy.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / NCD similarity): k-NN and kernel SVM with a normalised-compression-distance kernel over canonical SMILES; parameter-free, uncorrelated with ECFP Tanimoto, and ideal as a diversity component in a small-data ensemble.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / error-correcting output codes over related endpoints): train the three CYP-substrate tasks plus the three CYP-inhibition tasks as a 6-bit codeword per molecule and decode the target bit by minimum-distance decoding; inhibition data (12k molecules each) act as a large, legitimate auxiliary signal for the 667-molecule substrate tasks.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / belief propagation on similarity graphs): build a molecular similarity graph over train_val+test structures (structures only, no test labels) and run label propagation / graph-diffusion from the train labels; transductive diffusion is a well-matched estimator for scaffold-split tasks and runs in seconds.

Variance control: with 95-135 test molecules, the main lever is reducing prediction variance - average over many featurisations and many scaffold-grouped folds, and shrink probabilities toward the train prevalence where out-of-fold uncertainty is high.
targets.name: TDC ADMET small classification leaderboards (CYP substrates, hERG, DILI, Bioavailability): beat rank 1 on the official scaffold split

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on CYP3A4_Substrate_CarbonMangels (AUROC, live rank 1 0.667) - the weakest absolute record in the whole ADMET group.
The full strict win on CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels (AUPRC, live rank 1 0.474), where the positive class is small and the listed std is 0.025, so the bootstrap and 5-seed rules must both pass.

A calibration-only result: using a published or re-implemented baseline's raw scores, show that a declared post-hoc transform fit only on train_val out-of-fold predictions (e.g. isotonic/Platt or a prevalence-corrected ranking) raises the 5-seed AUPRC of that baseline above the live rank-1 value on one of the two AUPRC benchmarks, with the untransformed baseline reported alongside.

pitfalls: Tiny-test-set luck: 95-135 test molecules with 20-40 positives means the AUPRC/AUROC standard error is roughly 0.04-0.08. Any search over models selected on test will 'beat' these records; only out-of-fold selection on train_val plus the 5-seed, std-margin and bootstrap rules can distinguish signal from noise.

Metric swap: CYP2C9/CYP2D6 substrate are AUPRC while CYP3A4 substrate, hERG, DILI and Bioavailability are AUROC. Reporting AUROC where AUPRC is scored (or vice versa) looks like a large gain and is a pure artefact; use the group's own evaluate output.

Scaffold leakage via pretrained models and public AutoML pipelines: hERG, DILI and the CarbonMangels CYP sets are standard ingredients of ADMET pretraining collections, so a pretrained encoder may have memorised the test molecules' labels. Provenance must be declared and InChIKey overlap with test checked.

Label-noise/duplicate traps: the CarbonMangels substrate sets and the hERG set contain near-duplicate structures and some contradictory labels across sources; de-duplicating or 'cleaning' the OFFICIAL test rows (or dropping hard test molecules) invalidates the comparison entirely.

Threshold leakage: choosing a probability threshold, calibrating, or selecting an ensemble weight using the test labels. All calibration must be fit on train_val out-of-fold predictions only, and AUROC/AUPRC must be computed from raw scores.

Novelty trap: MiniMol, CFA, ZairaChem, ContextPred and newer 2024-2026 tabular/pretrained submissions report numbers on these same splits; a claim must beat the live rank-1 value AND any higher number published for the same benchmark in the last 24 months.
targets.statement: Six TDC ADMET classification benchmarks have fewer than 700 molecules, i.e. 95-135 test molecules, and their rank-1 scores sit far from ceiling: CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels (666 molecules, AUPRC, rank 1 MiniMol 0.474 +- 0.025, runner-up ZairaChem 0.441 +- 0.033), CYP2D6_Substrate_CarbonMangels (664, AUPRC, rank 1 ContextPred 0.736 +- 0.024), CYP3A4_Substrate_CarbonMangels (667, AUROC, rank 1 CFA 0.667 +- 0.019, runner-up MiniMol 0.663 +- 0.008), hERG (648, AUROC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.880 +- 0.002, runner-up CFA 0.875 +- 0.014), DILI (475, AUROC, rank 1 MiniMol 0.956 +- 0.006) and Bioavailability_Ma (640, AUROC, rank 1 MiniMol 0.942 +- 0.002). CYP3A4_Substrate at AUROC 0.667 and CYP2C9_Substrate at AUPRC 0.474 are barely above chance-plus, which is the signature of an under-attacked task rather than a solved one. The protocol is TDC's: official scaffold split from group.get(), 5 seeds, mean +- std from group.evaluate. Leaderboard pages are undated; the TDC repo's last commits are April 2025.
targets.success_criterion: Pick one dataset. Success means 5 saved prediction files (seeds 1-5 from tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group, no re-splitting, official test order, predicted probabilities in [0,1], manifest with sha256 of the test SMILES list and labels) such that (a) the test split is byte-identical to the group's own, (b) the mean of the dataset's OWN metric (AUPRC for the CYP2C9/CYP2D6 substrate sets, AUROC for CYP3A4_Substrate, hERG, DILI, Bioavailability) over the 5 seeds, recomputed by the skeptic through the group's evaluate call, is strictly HIGHER (direction: max) than the rank-1 value in the live leaderboard table for that dataset, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement exceeds max(listed rank-1 std, attacker's own 5-seed std) and is at least 0.015 absolute, (d) a stratified bootstrap over test molecules (10,000 resamples) puts the attacker's metric above the listed rank-1 value in at least 95% of resamples, and (e) only the official train_val rows of the same seed were used for fitting and threshold-free probabilities were produced (no test-label-dependent calibration), with any external data declared and InChIKey-disjoint from the test split.
targets.verification_method: PyTDC admet_group; group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5; hash-check the test SMILES and labels; load the attacker's 5 probability vectors; call group.evaluate to obtain the dataset's own metric mean/std; apply margin and bootstrap rules; re-fetch the live leaderboard page and parse every listed value. All six datasets are <700 molecules, so the skeptic can re-run the attacker's whole 5-seed pipeline in minutes on CPU and confirm the numbers from scratch.

angles: Make the genetic algorithm smarter, not bigger: Graph-GA with zero parameters is the record, so the headroom is in the search operators - fragment libraries mined from the best-scoring hits so far, adaptive mutation rates, crowding/fitness sharing to avoid premature convergence, and an explicit archive (MAP-Elites style) binned by scaffold and size so diversity and %Pass do not collapse the way Graph-GA's do.

Surrogate-assisted screening under a hard call budget: fit a cheap docking-score surrogate (fingerprint booster or Gaussian process) on the calls made so far and spend real oracle calls only on surrogate-predicted elites with high acquisition value - classic Bayesian optimisation over a discrete space, which the current leaderboard (one BO-free GA and four RL/VAE methods) never applied here.

CROSS-DOMAIN (cryptanalysis / key-space hill climbing with restarts): treat the molecular graph edit sequence as a key, run many short simulated-annealing climbs with tabu lists over recently tried fragments, and restart from an elite pool - the standard recipe for beating a plain GA in a rugged discrete landscape at a fixed evaluation budget.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / sphere packing in fingerprint space): maintain a covering code over fingerprint space so oracle calls are spent on mutually distant candidates (maximising information per call), which simultaneously raises the Diversity column that Graph-GA sacrifices.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / parallel tempering and population annealing): run several populations at different mutation 'temperatures' with periodic swaps, which escapes the local optima that fixed-rate GAs settle into.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / island biogeography and niche construction): island-model GA with migration between sub-populations defined by scaffold niches, with niche-specific selection pressure - a well-studied way to keep diversity while improving the best score.

Pose-quality filtering before counting a hit: re-score elites with a second, independent scoring function and discard molecules whose score depends on an implausible pose, which protects the %Pass and plausibility columns and avoids scoring-function exploitation.
targets.name: TDC Docking Benchmark Group (DRD3, 5,000-call docking oracle): beat the Graph-GA top-100/top-10/top-1 records

partial_wins.statement: Beat the live rank-1 Top100 value with the %Pass column no worse than the 'Best-in-data' reference row (Graph-GA's own %Pass is 0.393 +- 0.308, far below the data reference 0.780), i.e. a quality-constrained improvement rather than a raw-score one.
A budget-efficiency result: match or beat the live rank-1 Top10 value using at most half the claimed oracle budget, with the full call log proving the budget, verified by re-scoring the final top-10.

An oracle-reproducibility artefact: a documented, pinned docking-oracle configuration (receptor sha256, box, software version, seed) plus a re-scoring script under which a published method's released DRD3 molecules reproduce their reported scores to within 0.3 kcal/mol - a reusable verification harness, reported as infrastructure rather than a record.

pitfalls: Oracle mismatch: docking scores depend on the receptor file, box definition, exhaustiveness, software and seed. A 'record' computed with a different docking configuration than TDC's pyscreener DRD3 oracle is meaningless; the configuration must be pinned, hashed and reproducible by the skeptic, and scores must be reproduced within 0.3 kcal/mol.

Scoring-function exploitation (the classic docking false positive): GAs reliably discover huge, greasy, poly-aromatic or strained molecules that score extremely well and are physically nonsense. This is why the claim is void if %Pass drops below the 'Best-in-data' reference and why Diversity and M1 must be reported - Graph-GA's own %Pass of 0.393 shows the record itself is partly this artefact.

Oracle-budget cheating: calling the oracle during 'development' and then reporting only the final run's calls, caching scores across runs, or using a surrogate trained on out-of-budget oracle calls. The full ordered call log for each of the 3 runs, with repeated SMILES counted as TDC counts them, is the only acceptable evidence.
Single-run luck: Graph-GA's listed stds are large (0.3-0.4 kcal/mol on the score columns, 0.3 on %Pass), so one lucky run can beat the mean. Three seeded runs and the std-based margin are mandatory.

Column shopping: the table has Top100, Top10, Top1, Top1-P, Diversity, Novelty, %Pass and M1. Beating Top1 alone (a single lucky molecule) while Top100 is worse is not beating the benchmark; the claimed column must be stated and the others reported.

Novelty trap: this leaderboard is 2021-era while the molecular-optimisation literature (PMO/mol_opt and later work) has moved on; the NOVELTY skeptic must check whether better DRD3 docking-oracle results under the same budget are already published before anything is claimed.
targets.statement: The TDC Docking Benchmark Group defines a budgeted de novo design task: generate molecules with the best DRD3 docking scores using at most a fixed number of oracle calls (the leaderboard reports 5,000-call and smaller budgets), starting from ZINC 250K, with the oracle being a docking score computed through TDC's pyscreener wrapper. The leaderboard lists only five 2021-era generators plus a 'Best-in-data' reference row (Top100 -12.080, Top10 -12.590, Top1 -12.800, Diversity 0.864, %Pass 0.780, Top1-P -11.700, M1 5.100). Rank 1 is Graph-GA (a fragment-based genetic algorithm with ZERO learned parameters): Top100 -14.811 +- 0.413, Top10 -15.930 +- 0.336, Top1 -16.533 +- 0.309, Diversity 0.626 +- 0.092, %Pass 0.393 +- 0.308, Top1-P -14.267 +- 0.450; then SMILES-LSTM (-13.017 Top100), GCPN, MARS and MolDQN. That a parameter-free GA leads by 1.8 kcal/mol over a 3M-parameter LSTM, and that nothing has been added in years, is exactly the profile of a stale, beatable table; the oracle is CPU docking, so 5,000 calls is laptop-hours to laptop-days on 10 cores.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved generation record for the DRD3 benchmark at a declared oracle budget that the leaderboard reports (5,000 calls unless a smaller listed budget is explicitly claimed), consisting of: the full ordered log of every oracle call (SMILES plus returned score, length <= the budget), the final top-100 SMILES dictionary in the format the TDC docking group expects, the exact oracle configuration (pyscreener/docking software name and version, receptor file and its sha256, box centre and size, exhaustiveness, number of poses, random seed), and 3 independent runs with different seeds. It counts only if (a) the skeptic, re-running the SAME documented oracle configuration on the submitted top-100 SMILES, reproduces each molecule's score to within 0.3 kcal/mol, (b) the mean over the 3 runs of Top100 (and separately Top10, Top1) is strictly BETTER, i.e. more negative (direction: min), than the corresponding rank-1 value in the live leaderboard table at https://tdcommons.ai/benchmark/docking_group/drd3/ , re-fetched immediately before claiming, by at least the listed rank-1 std for that column, (c) the number of distinct oracle calls never exceeded the claimed budget (checked from the log, counting repeated SMILES as the benchmark does), (d) the submitted molecules satisfy the benchmark's own auxiliary filters as reported by the leaderboard columns - Diversity, %Pass (the medicinal-chemistry filter rate) and M1 are recomputed and reported, and the claim is void if %Pass falls below the 'Best-in-data' reference row's value, and (e) every submitted molecule is novel with respect to ZINC 250K (no InChIKey match) and chemically valid by RDKit with correct valences. No synthesis route, procurement information or experimental protocol is part of this target; the deliverable is a scored SMILES list only.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic installs the docking stack the attacker pinned (pyscreener plus the named docking binary), downloads the receptor from the attacker's manifest and checks its sha256, re-docks the submitted top-100 SMILES with the identical configuration on 10 CPU cores, compares each score to the attacker's log (tolerance 0.3 kcal/mol), recomputes Top100/Top10/Top1, Diversity, %Pass and M1 with TDC's own definitions, counts the oracle calls in the log against the budget, checks RDKit validity and ZINC-250K InChIKey novelty, then re-fetches the live leaderboard table and compares column by column. Re-docking 100 ligands is well under an hour on CPU; re-running the attacker's whole search is optional and is the laptop-days part.

angles: Replace the protein encoder with cheap sequence statistics: amino-acid composition, dipeptide/tripeptide k-mer counts with tf-idf, CTD (composition-transition-distribution) descriptors, pseudo-amino-acid composition, and binding-site-agnostic physicochemical profiles; concatenate with Morgan/FCFP fingerprints and train LightGBM with target-group-aware CV. This is the single most likely CPU win against a PLM ensemble.

Temporal domain adaptation done simply: sample-weight training pairs by patent recency (exponential recency weighting), or fit on the most recent years only, and calibrate the prediction distribution to the expected 2019-2021 affinity distribution; the leaderboard's own DomainBed baselines show elaborate invariance penalties (IRM 0.284) hurt, while trivial reweighting is untested.

CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / n-gram language models and alignment): score drug-target compatibility by an alignment-based kernel between the target sequence and the nearest-neighbour targets in the training set (Smith-Waterman similarity), then predict by similarity-weighted transfer of the ligand's affinities on those neighbours - a translation-by-analogy estimator that handles unseen targets.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / information distance): use normalised compression distance between protein sequences (and between SMILES) as a kernel for support-vector regression; NCD approximates an information-theoretic metric and needs no alignment, training or embedding model, and adds ensemble diversity for free.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ECOC and rank aggregation): discretise pAffinity into ordered bins with a Hadamard codebook of binary tasks, decode by minimum distance, and aggregate several decoders by Borda count; robust to the heavy label noise and unit heterogeneity of patent-derived affinities.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / free-energy additivity): model affinity as a sum of fragment-level contributions (ligand BRICS fragments x target residue-class indicators) with a sparse bilinear interaction term; group-lasso-regularised bilinear models are cheap and extrapolate better across time than black-box encoders.

Ensemble across structurally different models (booster on fingerprints, bilinear fragment model, k-NN by sequence similarity) with weights fit on a strictly temporal inner validation split (e.g. train on 2013-2016, validate on 2017-2018) to mimic the real shift instead of random validation.
targets.name: TDC DTI Domain-Generalization (BindingDB patent-year split): beat the listed Pearson correlation
